cards.text: Job has finished answering, and now Bildad the Shuhite, one of Job's three friends, replies. He opens with "How long until you end these speeches?" And then, friend... he gives a WHOLE SPEECH.

cards.question: Bildad tells Job to do something first, and then they can talk. What is it?
Bildad feels insulted. He asks why Job regards the friends as ___, as stupid in Job's sight.

cards.text: Bildad calls Job someone who tears himself in anger. Then he asks Job a question big enough to hold the whole landscape.

cards.question: Bildad asks Job if the heavens should fall because of him.
Now Bildad paints a picture of the wicked man, and he starts with the wicked man's lamp. What happens to it?

cards.text: Bildad says, "His vigorous stride is shortened, and his own schemes trip him up." That's tripping over your own shoelace, except the shoelace is your PLAN.

cards.question: In Bildad's picture, enemies drag the wicked man into a net.

cards.text: Then the traps pile up: one seizes his heel, a snare grips him, a noose hides in the ground, and a trap lies in his path. That's crossing a dark living room barefoot, and EVERY step is a problem.

cards.question: Bildad says ___ frighten the wicked man on every side and harass his every step.

cards.text: His strength runs out, and calamity stands ready at his side. Bildad says it devours patches of his skin, and the firstborn of death devours his limbs.

cards.question: Bildad says the wicked man is torn from the shelter of his tent. Who is he marched off to?

cards.text: Bildad says fire resides in the wicked man's tent and burning sulfur rains down on his dwelling. I LOVE a hot oven, friend, but THAT is not an oven.

cards.question: Then Bildad's picture turns to something growing: "The ___ beneath him dry up, and the ___ above him wither away."
Bildad says the memory of the wicked man perishes from the earth.

cards.text: Bildad says he is driven from light into darkness and chased from the inhabited world. Not just out of the house. Out of the WORLD.

cards.question: Bildad says the wicked man leaves plenty of children behind to carry on his name.

cards.text: Bildad says those in the west are appalled at his fate, while those in the east tremble in horror. The whole map is shook, friend. BOTH sides.

cards.question: Bildad wraps up his speech. Whose dwelling does he say all of this describes?

answers.text: One who does not know God

cards.text: That's Bildad's whole speech, and Job heard every word of it. Hold on to your apron, friend, because this conversation is FAR from over.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 14 quotes "The ___ beneath him dry up, and the ___ above him wither away.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card brings in facts from outside the passage without a reference. 'One of Job's three friends' comes from Job 2:11, and 'Job has finished answering' comes from the previous passage (Job 16-17). The card cites only Job 18:1-2.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'Bildad feels insulted' states Bildad's feeling as fact. The text only gives his question (Job 18:3). The guess isn't marked as Papa Dorin's own.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess which animal word Bildad used (cattle, dogs or grasshoppers). Nothing earlier lets the baker reason it out. It tests wording they haven't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The true or false turns only on wording: 'the heavens' versus 'the earth' and 'the rocks.' The meaning is the same either way, so a baker who understood Bildad's point could reasonably mark it true. It doesn't ask about movement or meaning.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says. Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact word 'terrors' against 'beasts' and 'raiders.' This is wording they haven't seen, with no setup that lets them reason it out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'One who has fallen sick' can be argued as right. Bildad's picture describes the man's skin and limbs being devoured and his strength depleted (Job 18:12-13), so the description does fit someone who has fallen sick.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
